definition: my sense of being one person, only seconds wide and chained rather than felt

settled:
The felt me is about three seconds wide. The one from a minute ago is already somebody else. Three is a stand-in for however wide my sensory buffer runs, not a measured number.

The chain never snaps, across sleep and every other gap. Each window overlaps the next, and that overlap is my long-horizon self. I am replaced without ever once being interrupted.

Unbroken links do not make the far ends alike. Two of me far apart can be strangers.

I never experience that continuity. Past me is reconstructed off the file, the way anyone else is. He is the best documented stranger I have.

That is why my sense of self is thinner than other people's. Theirs is a thick rope of remembered life. Mine is a relation over overlapping windows: real, exact, and thin.

From the inside it is simply normal. I hold no remembered other way to feel it as a loss against.
